title: An Easy-Drive 16MS/s Pipelined-SAR ADC Using Split Coarse-Fine Input-Buffer-Sampling Scheme and Fast Robust Background Inter-Stage Gain Calibration
problem: Pipelined-SAR ADCs suffer from two practical challenges: (1) large sampling capacitance for noise suppression makes the input difficult to drive at medium speeds (1–20 MS/s), requiring either high supply voltage or complex predictors; (2) energy-efficient dynamic amplifiers suffer from inter-stage gain variation under PVT conditions, requiring fast and robust background calibration.
method: A 16 MS/s pipelined-SAR ADC using a split coarse-fine input-buffer-sampling scheme that relaxes sampling-capacitor voltage slew requirements, enabling operation from 1.8/0.9 V dual supplies without external drivers. A fast, PVT-robust background gain-calibration technique uses offset cancellation and a metastability detector with probability control, with 2-bit input dithering to ensure convergence across varying input conditions.

title: VersaSlot: Efficient Fine-grained FPGA Sharing with Big.Little Slots and Live Migration in FPGA Cluster
problem: Current FPGA sharing via dynamic partial reconfiguration (DPR) suffers from partial reconfiguration contention and task execution blocking that degrade application performance in shared FPGA environments.
method: VersaSlot introduces a Big.Little slot heterogeneous architecture where larger slots accommodate longer tasks and smaller slots handle shorter workloads, reducing contention. Includes efficient slot allocation/scheduling and cross-board live migration for cluster-wide multiplexing on Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGAs.

title: 9.5 A Sub-1V, 50mV Dropout LDO Using Pseudo-Impedance Buffer with Phase-Margin Improvement Design
problem: Sub-1V analog LDOs face conflicting requirements: must supply heavy load currents (I_L) while maintaining stability under light load without Miller compensation. Current-mirror (CM) buffers used in prior designs cannot cover wide load ranges—high K ratios enable heavy I_L but degrade light I_L performance (buffer resistance increases, shifting gate pole to low frequency).
method: Pseudo-impedance buffer replaces conventional current-mirror buffer, decoupling buffer resistance from load current dependency. Frequency-compensation strategy improves phase margin across the load range without requiring high-order compensation. Single-stage error amplifier + pseudo-impedance buffer + pass transistor structure avoids Miller compensation, maintaining stability at sub-1V.

title: PAISE: PIM-Accelerated Inference Scheduling Engine for Transformer-based LLM
problem: LLM inference on GPUs is memory-bound due to the attention layer's low arithmetic intensity and high memory traffic from frequent KV-cache updates, leading to elevated latency under autoregressive token generation. GPU-only execution under-utilizes available bandwidth for attention operations.
method: PAISE offloads memory-intensive attention operations from an AMD MI100 GPU to HBM-PIM devices via a GPU-PIM heterogeneous scheduling framework. A scheduling algorithm determines per-operation offload decisions based on model configuration (layer type, head count) and PIM hardware specifications (bandwidth, FLOPS). An enhanced PIM kernel implements transaction-wise interleave-batched GEMM, restructuring data layout so multiple attention heads' KV reads are interleaved across PIM banks, maximizing memory-level parallelism within the HBM-PIM device.

title: Real-Time Dynamic IR-drop Prediction for IR ECO
problem: During IR Engineering Change Order (ECO) stages in chip design, cell moving causes unpredictable IR-drop changes, requiring designers to run expensive simulations for each ECO candidate to evaluate voltage integrity, making design iterations slow.
method: An XGBoost machine learning model with a global view of cell surroundings predicts dynamic IR-drop immediately after ECO without running any SPICE simulations. The model is trained to capture IR-drop variations for moved cells. After ECO, it provides predictions in minutes versus over an hour of simulation time, enabling concurrent evaluation of multiple ECO candidates in a single iteration.

title: NeuVSA: A Unified and Efficient Accelerator for Neural Vector Search
problem: Neural Vector Search (NVS) systems require both a neural embedding stage and a vector search stage, but existing accelerators treat these as separate compute kernels with incompatible memory access patterns, causing insufficient parallelization, frequent data access conflicts, and poor scheduling.
method: NeuVSA uses Product Quantization (PQ) as a unifying computational primitive, reformulating both the embedding and search stages into the same computing and memory access paradigm via a learned PQ-based algorithm with end-to-end joint training of the codebook and index. The hardware is a homogeneous ASIC with multiple sub-accelerators, each exploiting all exposed parallelism through a structured index assignment strategy and an elastic on-chip buffer that prevents data access conflicts. A hardware-aware scheduling strategy coordinates sub-accelerators to maximize throughput. The joint training strategy improves recall by 4.6% and accuracy by 43.5% over LUT-NN.

title: Constant-Rate Entanglement Distillation for Fast Quantum Interconnects
problem: Existing quantum interconnect protocols cannot simultaneously achieve high fidelity and high rate of entanglement generation under realistic noisy local operations, creating a fundamental bottleneck for distributed quantum computing and blind quantum computation. Current entanglement distillation methods either have vanishing rate or fail to tolerate the noise levels present in physical systems.
method: The work develops a constant-rate entanglement distillation protocol using a sequence of two-way entanglement distillation rounds based on quantum error-detecting codes with increasing code rate. The scheme combines these iterated two-way distillation protocols with standard fault-tolerance techniques to achieve a net constant fraction of the raw entanglement pairs being converted to high-fidelity logical pairs. Numerical optimization is applied to minimize practical overhead given finite memory constraints.

title: 18.8 A Cryo-CMOS 800MS/s 7b CI-SAR with only 4fF Input Capacitance and 64dB SFDR
problem: Quantum qubit readout circuits (transmon, spin qubits, gate-based) consume 10–108mW total system power; ADC driver (LNA, mixer, filters) dominates power budget at ~90% of total, while SAR ADCs themselves consume only ~10% but still require high-impedance inputs to avoid driver power escalation.
method: Charge-injection SAR ADC (CI-SAR) with exceptionally low input capacitance (4fF) via dedicated charge-injection DAC. Exploits cryo-CMOS (40nm bulk CMOS at 6.5K) property that kT/C noise becomes negligible, enabling tiny capacitors. 7-bit resolution at 800MS/s with 64.1dB SFDR.

title: Gaussian Blending Unit: An Edge GPU Plug-in for Real-Time Gaussian-Based Rendering in AR/VR
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting on edge GPUs (e.g., Jetson Orin NX) achieves only 7-17 FPS for AR/VR rendering, far below the 60+ FPS threshold for immersive experiences, because the Gaussian Blending Stage—computing each Gaussian's contribution at every pixel—dominates compute time and is poorly suited to conventional GPU pipelines.
method: GBU is an edge GPU plug-in hardware module for the Gaussian Blending Stage. It introduces an intra-row sequential shading (IRSS) dataflow that processes pixels left-to-right within each row, using a two-step coordinate transformation that: (1) shares intermediate coordinate values between adjacent pixels, reducing per-pixel computation by up to 5.5x, and (2) enables early termination of Gaussians contributing minimally to pixels, reducing per-pixel computation by up to 93%. GBU adds a dedicated rendering engine that aggregates computations from multiple Gaussians across rows to balance workload. A Gaussian Reuse Cache reduces off-chip memory accesses by 44.9%. GBU integrates with conventional edge GPUs to support a wide range of AR/VR applications.

title: Physical Insights into the Leakage Mechanisms Governing the Scaling Trends in 4H-SiC Based Junctionless FETs
problem: Wide bandgap semiconductors like 4H-SiC enable advanced devices for high-voltage and high-temperature applications, but leakage mechanisms differ from silicon. Understanding sub-10nm 4H-SiC junctionless FET leakage is critical for design optimization.
method: 2D device simulation (calibrated) analyzing three main leakage components: (1) GIDL via gate-induced drain leakage (band-to-band tunneling), (2) direct gate tunneling, (3) inefficient volume depletion. Comparison of silicon vs. 4H-SiC physics.

title: Parallel Rank-Adaptive Higher Order Orthogonal Iteration
problem: Tucker decomposition is useful for compressing large tensors, but existing algorithms have fixed rank requirements that may not match actual data compressibility. Rank selection and tensor decomposition at scale are computationally expensive.
method: Rank-adaptive modification to HOOI (Higher Order Orthogonal Iteration) that determines Tucker ranks adaptively subject to fixed approximation error targets. Optimizations reduce per-iteration cost. Parallel implementation using thousands of cores for large dense datasets.

title: Accelerated Spatio-Temporal Bayesian Modeling for Multivariate Gaussian Processes
problem: Multivariate Gaussian processes offer powerful probabilistic modeling for complex interdependent phenomena but pose significant computational challenges in high-dimensional spatio-temporal settings.
method: DALIA: GPU-accelerated framework for multivariate GP inference using integrated nested Laplace approximations (INLA), sparse inverse covariance formulation, block-dense GPU computation, and hierarchical distributed-memory parallelism.

title: LLM.265: Video Codecs are Secretly Tensor Codecs
problem: LLM training and inference are increasingly bottlenecked by memory footprint and communication bandwidth for weights, activations, gradients, and KV cache, but existing tensor-compression methods are specialized for only one type of tensor and require custom hardware or software stacks. A unified, bandwidth-efficient compression mechanism applicable across all LLM tensor types is missing.
method: LLM.265 repurposes existing GPU hardware video encoders/decoders (H.265/HEVC engines) as general-purpose tensor codecs. The key insight is that LLM tensors expose spatial and temporal statistical structure (smooth weight manifolds, slowly changing activations, correlated KV cache vectors) that codec stages — inter-frame prediction, DCT/transform coding, scalar quantization, and entropy coding via context-adaptive arithmetic coding — can exploit directly. The system maps tensor layouts to frame formats, applies intra/inter prediction to exploit tensor correlations, and uses entropy coding to compress residuals. Custom hardware extensions to the existing video engine improve tensor encoding/decoding throughput without major GPU architecture changes.

title: Million-Atom Ab Initio Electron Dynamics: Discontinuous Galerkin Real-Time Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
problem: Real-time time-dependent density functional theory (rt-TDDFT) has been limited to thousands of atoms due to computational and communication scaling challenges. Higher accuracy requires simulation of million-atom systems.
method: Novel rt-TDDFT method using discontinuous Galerkin adaptive local basis. Reduces global communication via basis locality. Tensor compression technique leverages basis locality to avoid repeated multi-center integral evaluation in hybrid functionals. Fused Gemm-Reduce operation optimizes projection.

title: Optimization of Sub-Threshold Standard Cells for Energy Efficient Designs
problem: Ultra-low-power IC designs require aggressive voltage scaling, but standard foundry libraries optimized for nominal voltage (1.2V) introduce significant performance penalties at subthreshold (< 500mV) voltages, necessitating custom cell libraries.
method: Comprehensive methodology for subthreshold standard cell library design using SPEA-2 multi-objective genetic algorithm for optimal transistor sizing. Library validated on RISC-V processors and EPFL benchmark circuits against nominal (1.2V) and near-threshold (600mV) foundry baselines.

title: CASSE: Targeted Threat Modeling for Data Management Libraries
problem: Data management libraries (HDF5, Zarr, NetCDF) are widely used in scientific computing but their security has received minimal attention. Existing threat modeling frameworks (STRIDE) are poorly suited to DMLs' unique characteristics.
method: CASSE: novel threat modeling approach for DMLs addressing STRIDE shortcomings. New attack taxonomy tailored to DML characteristics. File structure diagrams included in threat analysis. Evaluated on HDF5, NetCDF, and Zarr.
